title: Chapter 9.5 — Solving Quadratic Equations Using the Quadratic Formula

cards.back: $$ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $$ It gives the solutions of $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$.
The expression under the radical in the Quadratic Formula: $b^2 - 4ac$. It determines the number and type of solutions.
One real solution (one $x$-intercept, the vertex touches the $x$-axis).

cards.front: Determine the number of real solutions of $x^2 + 8x - 3 = 0$.
Determine the number of real solutions of $9x^2 + 1 = 6x$.
When is completing the square most efficient?
cards.back: When $a = 1$ and $b$ is an even number. The process involves fewer fractions.
When the quadratic expression can be factored easily into integer factors.

cards.front: When is the Quadratic Formula most useful?
cards.back: For any quadratic equation, especially when it is not easily factorable. It always gives exact solutions.

cards.front: Solve $x^2 + 11x - 12 = 0$ using the most efficient method.

cards.back: Not factorable over integers; completing square messy. $x = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{21}}{10}$.
